Pending Cases in high court

Writ petition cases, writ petition is an application filed before a Court, requesting to issue a specific writ. Whereas A writ means an order that is issued under an authority. Therefore, a writ can be understood as a formal order issued by a Court.

Second Appeal cases, second appeal can be filed against an judgement of the first appellate court. The Judgment passed by any appellate Civil Court in the first appeal can be challenged by way of a second appeal before the High Court.
First Appeal Cases, First Appeal lies to a superior court from a decree passed by a court exercising original jurisdiction.
Appeal Cases, An appeal case is when someone who loses a case in a trial court asks a higher court to review the trial court decision.
Petition cases, Petition cases are filed as a formal application to the court as a request of action on a particular case.

Revision Cases, Revision cases are action of revising, especially critically or careful examination or perusal with a view to correcting or improving. A High Court entertains a revision in any case decided by a subordinate Court in certain circumstances. This jurisdiction is known as revisional jurisdiction of the High court .

Reference cases, reference cases can only be made by a Court but not by a persona designate. Reference can be made by a subordinate court to state a case and refer the same for the opinion of the High Court. Such an opinion can be sought when the code itself feels some doubt about a question of Law.

Suit Cases, a civil suit begins when a legal person claims that he has been harmed by the actions of another person or business and asks the court for relief by filing a “complaint”. Most of the civil suits are guided by the well settled principles of the Code of Civil Procedure.
Review Cases, Review means to reconsider, to look again or to re-examine. In legal sense, it is a judicial re-examination of the case by the same court and by the same Judge.
Application cases, Applications are used to ask the court to make an order to resolve issues that come up in your case before the trial of the lawsuit.
